tour.title: Resurrection, Heaven, and What Happens to Your Body
tour.intro: This tour follows the New Testament’s own sequence: Jesus’s bodily resurrection as the pattern, the transformation—not abandonment—of your body, the intermediate hope of being with Christ after death, and the final horizon of resurrection and renewed creation. It distinguishes what the texts say clearly from what teachers acknowledge is less fully specified.

steps.why: Begin with the central category: the speaker calls 1 Corinthians 15 “the only chapter in the entire Bible whose topic from beginning to end is the resurrection from the dead,” setting bodily resurrection—not a vague afterlife—as the New Testament’s controlling question.

This clip works through Paul’s contrast between the present and future body: “It is sown a perishable body, but it’s raised an imperishable body.” It also explains that “spiritual body” does not mean immaterial, helping you hear what 1 Corinthians 15 actually claims about bodily transformation.

Now the tour addresses the timing question in 2 Corinthians 5. The teacher connects Paul’s “earthy tent” with the future “new resurrection body,” while emphasizing that if death comes before Christ returns, “that’s not the end of existence” and believers still await bodily renewal.

This is the clearest answer to the phrase “going to heaven.” The speaker surveys the New Testament glimpses of the dead being “with Jesus,” but stresses that this is not the permanent endpoint: believers are “awaiting their full redemption and recreation,” the New Testament’s larger hope.
steps.episodeTitle: Jesus, The Ultimate Heaven & Earth Meeting Place

steps.why: Finish with Philippians 3:20–21 and the destination of resurrection. Wright says, “Resurrection bodies belong on a renewed earth,” and explains that heavenly citizenship means awaiting Jesus to come and renew creation, not leaving earth permanently for a disembodied heaven.
steps.episodeTitle: What Did Jesus Mean By "My Father's House"? How should we think about euthanasia, and what are the rewards of Heaven?

tour.closing: The New Testament picture these clips assemble is neither “my body is discarded” nor simply “I go to heaven forever.” Death may mean being with Christ before the final resurrection, but the Christian hope is the resurrection of the body—transformed like Jesus’s—and life in God’s renewed creation.

caveats: Clips on ad-inserted hosts (Megaphone: ask-nt-wright, spoken-gospel) can land up to ~2 minutes off against today’s stream. This is a known corpus-wide drift, not a bug in this tour.
A tour is model output over machine transcripts. The "why" text should report what a transcript says; it is not a claim that the speaker is right.

The player streams each episode straight from its publisher. A few hosts (Substack’s CDN, for one) refuse hotlinked requests and the step will say so and offer the URL instead — the clip boundaries are still good, the playback path is not.
